### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-messaging`, touching **44** documentable anchor(s).

**45** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1cd47628e64beb49eec35ae77dcd3d049f5d010c`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 41 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **67** of **249** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1cd47628e64beb49eec35ae77dcd3d049f5d010c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `126eda98e7a8b51d4bc76bdc2e250a2ec3835c68` — the merge of head `621aa11e59e26ee578e05d2a999f54a1b8a486a6` into base `1cd47628e64beb49eec35ae77dcd3d049f5d010c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 126eda98e7a8b51d4bc76bdc2e250a2ec3835c68 && git checkout 126eda98e7a8b51d4bc76bdc2e250a2ec3835c68
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1cd47628e64beb49eec35ae77dcd3d049f5d010c 621aa11e59e26ee578e05d2a999f54a1b8a486a6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1cd47628e64beb49eec35ae77dcd3d049f5d010c && git merge --no-ff 621aa11e59e26ee578e05d2a999f54a1b8a486a6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1cd47628e64beb49eec35ae77dcd3d049f5d010c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1cd47628e64beb49eec35ae77dcd3d049f5d010c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**L1 verdict (L1-a): REWORK, one item, waiting on the seat's answer** at head `1c5040c142f65c8c25c0a45acd6f7c641833ca7f` (Fixes #35123, ruling B 7073270426 on top of 6996036362, declaration 7075520575, dev report 7075210312). This is a full read of `origin/main...1c5040c142`: 36 files, +898/−130.

## 席位核对

**Shape and gates** (`l1-face` CLEAN, 13 items):
- The PR is an open draft with `Fixes #35123` and no other closing keyword.
- Declarations: `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. One changeset covers service-messaging, app-shell and i18n as patches.
- CI: 61 success, 9 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending. `mergeable_state` is clean.
- No battery is owed: there is no `!` and no `(narrowing)` arm.
- Clause-② `no` reads right. The `digest` select accepts the same three values. `quiet_hours` was already free JSON. No export is added. The meaning change of a stored `none` is covered by the conversion.

**Against ruling B.** Items 1 to 6 are built as ruled.
- `digest` loses `defaultValue: 'none'`, and both field descriptions state the three states.
- `parseDigest` admits `none`, `parseQuietHours` reads `{ off: true }` (it wins over other keys), and both walks stop on `!== undefined`.
- The door answers an explicit off as `own`.
- The one-time conversion goes through a `sys_migration` claim made before the first rewrite, with a compare-and-set per row. It does not run without a ledger, and it is not the every-boot shape.
- The page offers "No digest" and saves a cleared window as `{ off: true }`. Save stays disabled until the window is touched, so opening the page writes nothing. The two notes are gone in 11 locales, and no reference to them is left.
- `packages/spec` is untouched.
- The changeset carries the ruling's "pick it again" sentence.
- The temporary hook is the seat's F2 from fork 7073430021. It has the carrier #36245 (open), and both the code and the PR body name it. `beforeInsert` runs once per row (`engine.ts:4796`), so a bulk insert is covered.
- Every pin the ruling lists is present. Ablations A1 to A8 each turned red, except A5, whose green result is explained. The integration file uses a real `ObjectQL` and `SqlDriver` on a file database across two boots.
- `field-types.mdx` is updated. I found no other published sentence this change makes false: the `protocol.mdx` digest rows describe the spec protocol schema, not this object.

**R1 (visible behaviour, so the seat's call; no code until it answers): an explicit "no quiet hours" also moves the member's digest to UTC midnight.**
- `preference-resolver.ts:225-227`: the digest window takes its time zone from the resolved quiet-hours row (`digestDeferral(cadence, nowMs, qh?.tz)`). ADR-0030 records this coupling at l.93-94: "digest windows currently use `quiet_hours.tz` → UTC".
- Here is the case. An organization sets daily digest and a 22:00-07:00 window with `tz: Europe/Berlin`. A member saves "no quiet hours" on the page. Their own row now decides quiet hours as `'off'`, `windowOf` returns no window, and their organization digest flushes at 00:00 UTC (01:00 or 02:00 Berlin) instead of Berlin midnight. Before this PR the member could not opt out, so the walk always reached the organization's window and its `tz`.
- No pin covers this, and neither the PR body nor the changeset says it.
- What could close it (the seat chooses, and per common.md it goes on to the maintainer if the seat reads it as a behaviour decision):
  - (a) Keep the behaviour as ADR-0030 already describes it. Add one pin, a sentence in the changeset and the PR body, and a carrier card for "digest time zone independent of quiet hours" (the ADR's deferred `sys_user` time-zone fallback has no card that I could find).
  - (b) Take the digest time zone from the next row that holds a window, past an explicit off. That is a code change plus a pin.
- Both choices are small. I have not picked one.

**Next.** The seat answers R1, and then a4-B makes the matching change. I read only that delta and give ACCEPT. After that, seat 7 runs the contract review, the seat adds the four pieces, and Leehom merges.

repo:objectstack#7 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jTeURPvEm465RcoYEC

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `621aa11e59e26ee578e05d2a999f54a1b8a486a6`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #35123 body and all 14 comments (rulings 6996036362 and 7073270426, forks 7073149058 and 7073430021, dev reports 7075210312 and 7076099772, claim revisions), PR #36326 body and all 8 comments (L1-a REWORK 7075548155, L1-a ACCEPT 7076146202), the net diff `c30ce97cd7..621aa11e59` (36 files, +942 −130; the merge base is current `main`), and the 74 check-runs on this head (63 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending).

### ① Derived judgments

The question is whether `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are true against the diff. They are. Each surface the diff moves:

- **`@objectstack/service-messaging` package index: unchanged, right.** `src/index.ts` is not in the diff. Its preference exports are named (`PreferenceResolver`, `PREFERENCE_OBJECT`, `quietHoursDeferral`, and the `Effective*` / `QuietHours` types), so the new `QUIET_HOURS_OFF` in `preference-resolver.ts` and the new modules `preference-digest-conversion.ts` and `preference-digest-unset.ts` are not reachable from the package entry. The PR body's "no export is added" holds.
- **Exported object `NotificationPreference`: a value change, not a shape change, right.** `digest` loses `defaultValue: 'none'`. The select still accepts exactly `none`, `daily` and `weekly`, and `quiet_hours` is still a free `Field.json`. No consumer in the repo reads `NotificationPreference.fields.digest`. Nothing that was accepted is refused, and nothing new is accepted, so there is no widening and no narrowing.
- **Data door for `sys_notification_preference`: same accept set, right.** A create that leaves `digest` out now stores and returns empty instead of `none`. What changes is the meaning of the stored `none`, which becomes the explicit off. That is a change of meaning on data, not on a contract shape. The changeset discloses it in full: the conversion, the "pick it again" sentence the ruling asked for, and the note that a hook-skipping write still stores `none`. `{ "off": true }` was already a valid JSON value. No server-side `quiet_hours` validator exists anywhere in `packages/` (grep at head), so nothing new is refused.
- **Door `effectiveFor` / `effectivePreferencesFor`: type unchanged, right.** `general.digest` stays `EffectiveSetting` of `'none' | DigestCadence`. `general.quietHours` stays `QuietHours | null`, because `windowOf` maps `'off'` back to `null`. Two value pairs become reachable that were not before: `none` with source `own`, and `null` with source `own`. Both fit the published type. The door itself came in with #34728, whose changeset `.changeset/34728-notification-settings.md` is still pending at this head (P4), so no release has published it.
- **`@object-ui/i18n` key surface: two keys narrowed, right to carry as `no`.** `notificationSettings.digestNoOff` and `notificationSettings.quietHoursNoClear` are removed from all 11 bundles. They came in with the same unreleased #34728 changeset, so no release ever carried them, and `git grep` at head finds zero references left. Locale dictionaries are also not a contract under the ADR-0150 reading (spec, protocol, SDK, a door's request or response).
- **`@object-ui/app-shell` `myPreferences.ts`: internal, right.** `OverridingDigest` is removed, `digestChoices()` drops its argument, `quietHoursSaveable` now also guards `null`, and `quietHoursStored` and `QUIET_HOURS_OFF` are added. The package is `private: true`, and its index does not re-export the module.
- **Translation bundles (`*.objects.generated.ts`): help text only, right.** Only the `help` strings of `digest` and `quiet_hours` change. Labels and option keys are unchanged.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`: right.** `sys_notification_preference` rows are data. The object definition is a shipped system object, not something a metadata author writes. `packages/spec` is untouched (ruling item 6), and so is the spec's `NotificationPreferencesSchema` (`api/protocol.zod.ts`), which is a separate layer. `Spec property liveness` and `Check Changeset` are success.
- **Against ruling 7073270426.** Items 1 to 6 are built as ruled: three states per field; `digest` without a default; `{ "off": true }` as the marked value the ruling leaned towards; a one-time conversion claimed in `sys_migration` before the first rewrite; page, resolver and locales changed in one PR; `packages/spec` untouched. Every pin the ruling lists is present. The L1 R1 rework holds. `resolveDigestZoneWindow` walks the same four rows as `resolveQuietHours`, stops only at a row that holds a window, and is pinned with a UTC control. ADR-0030 l.93-94 still reads true.

S1 (should-fix) — the one-time conversion can rewrite a `none` chosen after the fix is live. In `preference-digest-conversion.ts`, the pass re-reads `where: { digest: 'none' }` after each batch until no unseen row is left. The compare-and-set only checks that the row still holds `none`. So during the pass, any row that newly holds `none` is also rewritten to empty: a new row inserted with an explicit `none`, or a snapshot row whose member re-picks `none`. So is a row written with `none` by a not-yet-upgraded node in a rolling deploy. The window is the length of the boot pass, so it is narrow, but it is exactly what the ruling's item 4 forbids ("⛔ … from then on `none` is a member's real choice"). Fix: take the id set before the claim and rewrite only that snapshot (page by an id cursor instead of re-reading the filter). That also covers the dev's own Acceptance note: when the claim fails, the next boot can convert a `none` written in between. **Non-blocking: it can be carried on a follow-up card** together with that note. Nothing in this head makes it worse after the pass.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/35123-member-digest-quiet-hours-opt-out.md`: `patch` for `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/i18n`. These are exactly the three released packages the diff moves. `content/docs/**` and `docs/audits/**` publish nothing.
- With `Metadata-protocol: none` and no widening or breaking arm, `patch` is the level AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist 3) prescribes for a bug fix in a released package. No BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 marker is owed.
- `Clause-②: no` is line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body, and it is true for the reasons in ①. `Check Changeset` is success at this head (rerun after the 07:4xZ body edit).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev `open_questions`.** Report 7076099772 has none. The two earlier forks are answered on the card. 7073149058 was answered by ruling 7073270426 (B, one PR). 7073430021 was answered by the seat's F2, with F1 carried by #36245.
- **Dev flag: interim `beforeInsert` hook, carried by #36245.** Answered. #36245 is open, p1, `domain:server`. Its body says "When this card merges, remove that hook and its pin in the same PR", and the code comment and the changeset both name it. A hook-skipping write (raw SQL, a bulk load) still stores `none` on a legacy database until #36245 lands. That is disclosed in the PR body and the changeset, and accepted as the interim.
- **Dev flag: no "follow the organization again" action on the page.** Accepted for this card: the ruling did not ask for one, and the Setup grid can clear the field. Recommended as a follow-up card. Without it, a member who once saves a digest or quiet hours from the page cannot go back to following the organization from the page.
- **Dev flag: a failed claim after the read lets the next boot convert a `none` written in between.** Folded into S1 above, on the same follow-up card.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5).**
  - The conversion materialises ids (`fields: ['id', 'organization_id']`, ≤ 10000 per read) and then updates row by row. A grouped `update … where digest = 'none'` per organization would push down. A reason is given in the code: each write threads the row's own organization as `tenantId` and compares-and-sets by id. It follows the precedent `preference-user-conversion.ts`, and the tenant-audit census rows were regenerated for it. Reason given, so no finding.
  - `resolveDigestZoneWindow` adds no query: it walks the in-memory index `loadRows` already holds.
- **Gates.** All derived families are answered by the check-runs on this head: 63 success, 0 failed. Of the 11 skipped, `18.x upgrade harness (opt-in)` is opt-in. The legacy physical DEFAULT `none` it would exercise is pinned instead by the two-boot file-database integration test (`preference-digest-three-states.integration.test.ts`, real `ObjectQL` + `SqlDriver`).
- **Ungraded note.** `QUIET_HOURS_OFF` is spelled twice, in `preference-resolver.ts` and in `ui/…/myPreferences.ts`, and no pin ties the two together. Optional; it can ride the same follow-up card.
- **Escalations.** None.

No must-fix. One should-fix (S1), non-blocking and carried on a follow-up card.

  - L1-a ACCEPT 7076146202.
  - Contract PASS 7076382062 by seat repo:objectstack#7 (`TIER_DEFAULT`), with no must-fix. Its one should-fix, S1, is graded by that record as non-blocking and carried on a follow-up card.
